summary: Staggered zero-length stream chunks and missing terminal choice after auth token swap behind corp proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on BrightChat (dedicated account) intermittently observe streaming responses where the client receives a sequence of zero-length SSE chunks (":
") interleaved with valid tokens, then the stream ends without the terminal choice/event. This appears to correlate with short-lived auth token rotation (customer side) + corporate reverse proxy that does TLS offload and HTTP header rewrite.

Impact:
- Affected sessions drop the final sentence/closing JSON object ~7-15% of long-running streaming responses for >1024 token generations.
- User-visible: truncated replies or missing closing metadata (finish_reason/stop).
- Customer complains of degraded UX and reports increased retries.

Environment:
- BrightChat dedicated cluster in us-east (dedicated pool mapping to rdx-ded-us-east-3).
- Using SSE streaming endpoint /v1/streams with API gateway behind corporate reverse-proxy (client -> corp-proxy -> BrightChat edge).
- Client rotates local auth cookie/token every ~30s as part of their SSO flow.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long generation (approx > 800 tokens) via SSE from a browser behind corporate proxy that performs header rewriting and TLS termination.
2) Trigger an auth token refresh mid-generation (they do a silent refresh on background tab); the client sends a new Authorization header value to the proxy.
3) Observe stream output: sequences of zero-length SSE events appear (i.e., empty data lines), occasionally followed by valid data chunks, then the stream ends with no terminal 'done' event or final metadata.
4) Re-establishing a fresh connection returns the remainder of generation only ~40% of the time (lossy).

Logs & snippets:
- Edge logs show repeated 200-hits for frame chunks but occasional short-lived TLS session renegotiation around the token swap windows.
- Proxy (customer-side) config shows header rewrite for Set-Cookie + Authorization passthrough.
- Sample client capture attached in ticket (browser devtools HAR): contains multiple "data:

" SSE events and final connection CLOSE without server-sent 'event: done'.

Repro rate: ~0.12–0.18 per long session in their workload; higher when client token refresh aligns with generated tokens >1024 sequence lengths.

Workaround used by customer:
- Short-term: reduce token rotation frequency on client side (~every 5min) or disable silent refresh during active streaming sessions.
- Customer has also implemented a client-side re-request that attempts to patch missing final chunk by sending last n tokens as context, but it is not robust and increases cost.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Corp-proxy rewrites and short-lived re-auth cause a sequence of half-closed TCP/TLS frames that the edge gateway translates into empty SSE data lines when the request body is in-flight.

Hypothesis 2: API gateway currently treats a client TLS renegotiate/conn-replacement as a soft socket event and emits keepalive/empty chunks; downstream streaming framing logic misinterprets this and suppresses terminal 'done' when final bytes race with socket close.

Evidence: Worker stdout shows the final 'done' JSON emitted and flushed at time T, but gateway-to-edge logs show a socket reset during T+10–60ms. The HAR capture shows a final CLOSE without trailing 'event: done' chunk in the wire.

Reproduction: Created a test harness that rotates Authorization header midstream (client simulated), proxied through an NGINX instance that does header rewrite. Reproduced empty data events and missing final event in 30% of runs when TLS session reused across keepalive and token swap.

Priority trace: Edge gateway increments 'stream-restart' counter when soft socket swap occurs; current code path does not queue final terminal event when connection handoff occurs during in-flight flush.
next_steps: Add logging at gateway layer to tag when we detect mid-stream Authorization header changes and TLS session renegotiation; capture timing between final worker flush and socket close.
Engineering: implement a short (100ms) grace-window at gateway to buffer terminal events on socket handoff and attempt a second-write before declaring stream closed.
Auth/Docs: advise customers in Dedicated runbooks to avoid client-side token rotation during active streaming or to use long-lived session tokens for streaming flows.
SRE: add dashboard alert for 'stream-terminal-missing' correlated with proxy reauth events in customer accounts.
Follow-up ticket: create INT-642000 to track gateway buffering change and testing matrix across proxies (NGINX, F5, Azure-ALB).
resolution: In progress: temporary mitigation documented to customer (delay token rotate during active streams). Engineering has PR to add a short buffer window in the gateway to attempt to flush terminal events on mid-stream handoff (WIP). Full fix pending validation across proxy types.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Temporary workaround accepted by BrightChat; drop rate reduced to ~1%.
2026-03-12 - Engineering PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4271 (adds 100ms terminal-event buffer and retries write on soft socket swap).
Test plan: run synthetic harness across NGINX/Cloudflare/Corp-F5 with token-swap timing variance and validate terminal-event success >99.9% on long-form streams.
